findings.title: PWAInstallPrompt unguarded setTimeout — lifecycle gap
findings.why_it_matters: setShowPrompt(true) could fire on unmounted component if user navigates away within 2 seconds of beforeinstallprompt — RESOLVED this loop.
findings.what_is_wrong: apps/web/src/components/PWAInstallPrompt.tsx:49 — setTimeout(() => setShowPrompt(true), 2000) with no clearTimeout in useEffect cleanup at lines 61-65.
findings.why_weakens_submission: Unguarded timer is a lifecycle hazard; sets state on unmounted component.
findings.minimal_correction_path: Store timer ID; call clearTimeout in cleanup. Resolved this loop.

simplification_check.structurally_necessary: PWAInstallPrompt cleanup — setTimeout at line 49 without clearTimeout in useEffect return is a React lifecycle gap; fix stores timer ID and calls clearTimeout in cleanup. Deletion test: n/a (adding cleanup, not removing module).

builder_notes.pattern: useEffect with setTimeout but no clearTimeout in cleanup
builder_notes.how_to_recognize: setTimeout(...) inside useEffect setup with no corresponding clearTimeout in the return function; timer ID not stored anywhere
builder_notes.smallest_coding_rule: Every setTimeout inside useEffect must have its ID stored and cleared in the cleanup return.
builder_notes.stack_example: PWAInstallPrompt.tsx:49 — unguarded; fix: let showTimer = setTimeout(...); cleanup: if (showTimer !== null) clearTimeout(showTimer)

builder_notes.pattern: validateTiersShape(_tiers) { return true } — always-true stub is a dead-code seam
builder_notes.how_to_recognize: Function whose body is return <literal>; doc-comment says 'TypeScript typing enforces most invariants'
builder_notes.smallest_coding_rule: If the function always returns a constant, delete it or implement it honestly.
builder_notes.stack_example: packages/core/src/tierLogic.ts:75-77 — stub preserved for API compatibility but enforces nothing

builder_notes.pattern: 5-selector dep cluster shared across N handlers — identical dep arrays signal extraction
builder_notes.how_to_recognize: When 3+ useCallback blocks list the same 4+ state selectors in their dep arrays, they belong in a single hook reading selectors internally
builder_notes.smallest_coding_rule: Same 4+ deps in 3+ callbacks = one hook.
builder_notes.stack_example: handleExportJSON, handleExportCSV, handleExportMarkdown all had [projectName, tierOrder, tierLabels, tierColors, tiers] — identical dep arrays exposed the cluster.
